questions.q: What did Woz's father do that helped shape his passion for electronics?
a: He brought Steve to work and explained physics in kid-friendly ways
He bought Steve his first factory-built personal computer
He enrolled Steve in a private school for young engineers
He hired tutors to teach Steve programming after class
questions.why: Lesson 1 says his father took him to work and explained physics with simple diagrams and stories.

questions.q: When Woz found his college computer course taught only FORTRAN, what did he do?
a: He taught himself six other programming languages
He switched his major to mathematics instead
He asked the department to add several new courses
He dropped out to work at a computer company
questions.why: Lesson 2 says FORTRAN was not enough, so he learned and experimented with six more languages.

questions.q: What was the Cream Soda Computer?
a: A working computer Woz built himself from a circuit board
A software program he sold to his university
A video game he designed for a science fair
A kit he assembled together with his father
questions.why: Lesson 2 says it was really just a circuit board, but still an actual, usable computer he built.

questions.q: Which values does the summary say Woz adopted in childhood?
a: Fairness, honesty, kindness and a good sense of humor
Ambition, competition, discipline and thrift
Loyalty, patience, piety and modesty
Curiosity, independence, courage and thrift
questions.why: Lesson 1 lists these as the values that shaped his later way in life.

questions.q: How did Woz treat his early Apple shares?
a: He sold them to early employees for five dollars each
He held every share until the company went public
He traded them for a management position at Apple
He donated all of them to his former university
questions.why: Lesson 3 says he gave ten million dollars of shares to early employees for five dollars apiece.
